h: Yosef Called "Kol": The Order of the Ushpizin

p: when it reckons the seven Musaf offerings
and it is called Musaf Shabbos,
that the middah of Yosef is called Kol?
that we translate "for all in heaven and on earth"
as "which holds on to heaven and earth."
בְּיִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ, ו׳ ה׳,
in the unification of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah, vav and hei,
And likewise there are upper heavens
and as is written in the holy Zohar
and the letter vav is "the middle bar
and it is the middah of Yaakov,
"who holds on to Atika Kadisha," etc.,
as they said in the holy Zohar
הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף,
who is the small vav — the filling,
and as they said in the holy Zohar
"and the two of them go together,
and this is the secret of the letter vav-vav,
for the two go together," etc.
And this is why it says that Musaf Shabbos —
the addition of holiness from Shabbos,
which is the middah of Malchus —
Tzaddik, Yesod Olam, who is called Kol,
and through him the drawing-down from Atika
down to the hei — the lower Shabbos.
And this is why it says
And this is the matter of the Ushpiza of Yosef,
which is the preparation for Hoshana Rabbah,
which is a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
is the drawing-down from all the middos to Malchus,
how could there be a drawing-down
even of the holiness of Moshe and Aharon,
is a chariot for the Name Havayah,
and all the middos were included in his body,
as they are reckoned in Pesach Eliyahu
And this is what it says in the Midrash
"'And he touched the hollow of his thigh'
he touched the righteous men and women,
who were destined to come from him," etc.
he said that in his offspring there was still
that they had not yet been refined
in the middah of "truth to Yaakov."
meaning that he was healed of his limp
to the middah of Knesses Yisrael —
even the holiness of Moshe and Aharon,
who are a chariot for the middos of Netzach and Hod,
from where the prophets draw their nourishment —
even though they were not yet born,
And this is what it says in the holy Zohar
if the Shechinah, who is called Ani,
that place which is called Kol
And although Kol is the middah of the tzaddikim,
only when there is the resting of the Shechinah
and the union of HaKadosh Baruch Hu —
then the middah of Kol is here,
for the drawing-down is through the middah of
Tzaddik, Yesod Olam, who is called Kol,
and it is the vav of the filling,

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldos — "On Shabbos, corresponding to the Tzaddik, Yesod Olam, who is called Kol (All), and it is called Musaf Shabbos, to add to it delights from the hidden brain; and on Rosh Chodesh, corresponding to Knesses Yisrael, who is called the moon."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 7 — “And this is according to what is said in the Zohar Chadash (Ki Sisa): ‘Remember the day of Shabbos’ — in the secret of the covenant, which is Yesod, to which Yosef holds; and therefore it is called Shabbos, for Yosef is called Kol, and Shabbos too is called Kol; and so it says (there, end of Toldos) that the Musaf of Shabbos corresponds to the tzaddik, foundation of the world.” Connection: Both bring the Zohar Chadash that Yosef is called “Kol” and corresponds to the Musaf of Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, Addenda — "And come and see: Hillel the Elder, when he rejoiced at this celebration, said: If I am here, all is here; and if I am not here, who is here? He was hinting and saying: if the Shechinah, who is called 'I' (Ani), dwells here, all is here — that place called 'all' (kol), which comes to unite with her; and if I am not here, who is here — for there is no complete good, since the Shechinah does not dwell in the Holy Land."

p: However, in the siddur Shaar HaShamayim
the order of the Ushpizin is given as:
the Avos, Yosef, Moshe, Aharon, David,
And seemingly this is contrary to what is explicit
in several places in the holy Zohar
in the order of the seven shepherds:
Yosef is a chariot for the middah of Yesod Olam,
and like the order of the Ushpizin
But in truth it is found
corresponding to the level of Yosef;
corresponding to the level of Moshe;
corresponding to the level of Aharon."
And in truth, also in the Zohar Chadash
which reckons the order of the shepherds
as a chariot for the middos,
as a chariot for the middah of Yesod —
when it reckoned the seven shepherds,
it reckoned the forefathers of the world:
And in truth, these and these
are the words of the living God,
for there is support also for this order,
for on the fourth day the luminaries were hung,
which were from the primordial light,
and it is written, "Light is sown for the tzaddik"
"'And the Netzach' — this is the downfall
for Esav falls by his offspring.
corresponding to the level of Moshe,"
for it is brought in the holy Zohar
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רכג, ב, פִּנְחָס):
"and He gave the Hod to Moshe,
as it says, 'You shall place some of your majesty upon him'"
And so it is in the Tikkunim
the skin of his face shone."
And so it is in the Tanchuma
And it reckons "on the sixth day
corresponding to the level of Aharon,"
"Aharon is the groomsman of the Matronisa," etc.,
and he is the one who atones for and purifies
and this is the middah of Kol,
But the difference between the two views
of Rav Huna and Rav Chisda
one says, "With Me is the lowly,"
and one says, "I am with the lowly."
That is, according to the one who says
Aharon is reckoned as the middah of Kol,
And according to the one who says "I am with the lowly,"
Yosef is the sixth middah — Kol,
And so is the reckoning of the Ushpizin
and as they said in the Gemara (ibid.):
"And it is more reasonable like the one who says
which corresponds to David, the King Mashiach,
for then will come the great salvation —
(And what it says in the holy Zohar
the order is "I am with the lowly,"
and Hod, the level of Aharon,
is in the Chessed of Avraham.
And after the days of the Chag pass,
the level of Aharon holds on to
which brings them close to Torah
to Hashem, may He be blessed,
like the one who says "With Me is the lowly";
and these and these are the words of the living God.
So I heard within the holy chamber.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldos — Corresponding to the seven supernal days, He created on earth seven true tzaddikim, each corresponding to his day, the fathers of the world: Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Yosef, Moshe, Aharon and David; they are called "the ancient mountains," for they depend on those seven supernal days — the six days of Bereishis and the seventh that stands before them; as it says, "And the house of David shall be like God" (Zecharyah 12:8).

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a — "When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear,' sixty myriads of ministering angels came and tied two crowns on each one of Israel… When they sinned, they were taken off… R. Rashi: crowns from the radiance of the Shechinah; ohel in the sense of "when His lamp shone (b'hilo)," the radiance of Moshe's face.

Our Rabbis said: from the cave, as it says, 'And I will place you in the cleft of the rock' (Shemos 33:22) — the Holy One placed His palm upon him, and from there he merited the rays of glory. paragraphs.text: Sotah 5a — “'And with the crushed and lowly of spirit': Rav Huna and Rav Chisda differed. One said: 'The crushed one is with Me'; the other said: 'I am with the crushed one.' It is more reasonable to follow the one who says 'I am with the crushed one,' for the Holy One, blessed be He, left all the mountains and hills and rested His Shechinah upon Mount Sinai; Mount Sinai did not rise upward.” The preferred reading describes the Shechinah descending to the humble, rather than the humble being physically raised. It supplies the specific meaning of 'I am with the crushed one' used here.
